title: Zoom in: posting a payment, from BEGIN to a durable commit
caption: One invoice row is locked for a few milliseconds; the commit waits for exactly one thing, the standby's WAL flush.

messages.label: BEGIN
messages.note: Transaction mode: PgBouncer lends a server connection for this transaction only.

messages.label: SELECT invoice … FOR UPDATE
messages.note: Locks the one invoice row (INV-4471, 1 250.00 due). The tenant's other invoices stay free.

messages.label: UPDATE invoice: due − 400.00
messages.note: CHECK (amount_due >= 0) on the row refuses an overpayment.

messages.label: INSERT ledger: Dr cash, Cr AR
messages.note: Two rows in this month's ledger partition, sharing one journal id.

messages.label: COMMIT
messages.note: A deferred constraint trigger checks that the journal's debits equal its credits, then the commit record goes to the WAL.

messages.label: WAL up to the commit record
messages.note: Streaming replication; the payment is not confirmed yet.

messages.label: flushed
messages.note: About a millisecond in the same region: the price of losing no confirmed payment.

messages.label: COMMIT ok
messages.note: The row lock is released now.

messages.label: payment posted
messages.note: The server connection goes back to the pool for the next transaction.

scenarios.name: Two payments at once
scenarios.summary: A bank-feed match and a manual entry hit the same invoice: the row lock serialises them, and the second sees the first's result.

messages.label: T1: SELECT invoice … FOR UPDATE
messages.note: The bank-feed matcher locks INV-4471.

messages.label: T2: SELECT invoice … FOR UPDATE
messages.note: A clerk records the same payment by hand. T2 waits for T1's lock.

messages.label: T1: UPDATE due → 0; ledger; COMMIT
messages.note: T1 commits; the lock is released.

messages.label: T2: row (due = 0)
messages.note: Read Committed re-reads the locked row after the wait, so T2 sees the new balance, not the old one.

messages.label: T2: UPDATE due − 1 250.00
messages.note: Would make amount_due negative.

messages.label: CHECK violation
messages.note: T2 rolls back as a whole: no ledger rows, no half-posted payment.

messages.label: 409: already paid
messages.note: The API offers to record it as unapplied credit instead.

scenarios.name: Standby unreachable
scenarios.summary: With one sync standby and nothing else, commits wait forever when it disappears; a quorum of two standbys (ANY 1) keeps payments posting.

messages.label: COMMIT
messages.note: Same payment as before; the commit record is written locally.

messages.label: WAL up to the commit record
messages.note: The standby's host has just lost its network.

messages.label: wait for a standby flush
messages.note: The invoice row stays locked, and other payments on it queue behind.

messages.label: timeout
messages.note: The API can't tell whether the payment committed; it must check before retrying.

messages.label: ANY 1 (sb1, sb2): sb2 flushed
messages.note: With synchronous_standby_names = 'ANY 1 (sb1, sb2)' one standby can be lost without stopping commits.

scenarios.name: Unbalanced entry
scenarios.summary: A buggy close job writes a debit without its credit: the deferred check fails at COMMIT and nothing from the transaction survives.

messages.label: BEGIN
messages.note: A month-end accrual job opens a transaction.

messages.label: INSERT ledger: Dr expense 90.00
messages.note: A code bug forgets the matching credit line.

messages.label: row checks pass
messages.note: Each row is valid on its own; balance is a property of the whole journal.

messages.label: COMMIT
messages.note: The deferred constraint trigger fires now, once per inserted ledger row; each firing checks that its row's journal sums to zero.

messages.label: debits ≠ credits
messages.note: The whole transaction rolls back. The ledger never shows an unbalanced journal, whoever wrote it.
